_comment: Text to music with ACE-Step 1.5 turbo: MIT, and its model card allows commercial use of what it makes. The sampler settings are the official ComfyUI template's: 8 steps at cfg 1.0, euler with the simple scheduler, AuraFlow sampling shift 3, and a zeroed negative (the model takes no negative prompt). Put a caption in Music.tags and [Instrumental] in Music.lyrics for a track with no singing. Music.duration and Length.seconds are separate inputs that nothing ties together: set both to the same length. THE PLANNER IS OFF HERE (Music.generate_audio_codes false), and anything with a tune should turn it on: its 1.7B language model writes codes that carry the melody and the orchestration, and a menu theme, a chamber piece and two battle tracks made without it were rejected by ear, while ambient beds held up. With only [Instrumental] in Music.lyrics it lays the track out as a song, with an intro, breaks and an ending; with a section script there instead ([Main Theme - strings], [Variation - horns], no intro, breakdown or outro) six battle takes of six held together. A slow theme still fell silent for half a minute; the same theme as a march over an ostinato did not. It is slow: about 4.5 minutes on the CPU for 150 seconds of music. THE TEXT ENCODERS RUN ON THE CPU ON PURPOSE: on this image's PyTorch 2.6 the planner's sampling on the GPU produces NaN probabilities, and the CUDA assert aborts the whole ComfyUI server, taking every queued job with it (Comfy-Org/ComfyUI#12274). On the CPU it works, at about 2.3 s of planning per second of music. Saves FLAC, so the loop and encode step works from lossless audio. Needs the 'music' weight group. scripts/generate_music.py drives this from a prompt folder.

inputs.tags: <<< CAPTION: the genre, then a sentence or two on mood, instruments and pace >>>
